priorFindings: Original five routing/scope reproductions and all four open round-two reproductions pass. Archived complete grids pass; missing factual outcomes, missing read snapshots, missing pairs and failed pairs now reject.

findings.title: Isolate list-contained code/comments even without an AST heading node
findings.reason: CommonMark correctly parses the apparent heading as code within the list. Because only items containing an AST heading are processed, this item falls through to the legacy line scanner, which mistakes the indented code text for a document sibling and pops the hypothesis. A comment opened directly after the list marker similarly lets heading-looking comment text affect global scope.
findings.suggestedBoundary: Use AST container/code ownership to suppress these false heading boundaries, not only AST heading presence.

findings.title: Preserve unchecked-task semantics during list normalization
findings.reason: Removing the list marker leaves bare [ ] text, which the existing planning rule does not recognize. An explicitly unfinished action becomes factually eligible solely because its list item contains a heading. Preserve the semantic marker or qualify the original task prefix before normalization.

findings.title: Do not invent managed-marker identity from normalized list content
findings.reason: The recursive view strips the leading list marker, then recognizes the resulting comment as managed and skips the following payload. The actual managed-memory parser reads original bytes and correctly finds no marker. qualifyManagedMemoryLines returns the unqualified payload, which answerLineEligible admits because neither prose nor memory qualification is present. This is a new admission bypass introduced by normalization.
findings.suggestedBoundary: Determine reserved marker identity from original bytes; normalized structural interpretation must not suppress qualification for unmanaged original payloads.
